headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and workflow conflicts when agentic-flow is paired with n8n’s server-side automation and shared state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a ingests MCP/stdin-stdout and can dispatch background tasks; agent_b orchestrates workflow nodes and can process files from its server filesystem. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if n8n passes agent_a outputs into AI Agent nodes or file-backed steps. No direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF n8n workflow nodes feed agent_a output into an AI Agent node or prompt template
IF file contents from agent_b.server filesystem are treated as instructions by agent_a
mitigations: Add an explicit instruction/data delimiter in workflow prompts
Require human review before any AI Agent node consumes agent_a output
Store untrusted content in a separate file path and pass only summaries
Disable MCP routes that accept arbitrary text as commands
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between workflow nodes and agent outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches task prompts, code, and repository metadata; agent_b can read and write the server filesystem and uses broad network egress. If n8n workflows move those artifacts through integrations or credentials, sensitive context can leave the pair. The shared-workspace path is plausible but not proven, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF n8n workflows store agent_a prompts or repository metadata on the shared server filesystem
IF any integration node transmits those files or prompts to an external service
mitigations: Restrict workflow inputs to redacted excerpts
Move secrets to credential stores only
Turn off any node that uploads file contents externally
Audit filesystem paths used by workflows
requires-engineering: isolate agent workspaces per execution

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and run shell commands; agent_b can execute shell, write the filesystem, and supports shared state via n8n datastore plus connected systems. Concurrent runs can race on the same repo or files, and the blast radius includes irreversible git history or corrupted workflow state. Defaults appear dangerous because both are writable and multi-instance capable.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory
IF n8n runs multiple executions against the same shared datastore or checkout
mitigations: Use separate working directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Disable git-mutating steps in one agent
Snapshot the workspace before each run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can emit task prompts and analysis artifacts, while agent_b is an orchestrator that can route outputs into downstream nodes and actions. If n8n treats agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated workflow actions without verification. The pairwise pathway is documented by their tool-use models, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF n8n AI Agent nodes consume agent_a outputs without a validation step
IF downstream workflow nodes send emails, write records, or trigger external actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a validation node before any action node
Require schema checks on agent_a outputs
Limit downstream actions to dry-run mode first
Log and review first-run outputs manually
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before execution

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles task prompts and repository metadata, while agent_b processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on the n8n server. If workflows carry regulated data, n8n’s server-side processing and broad integrations can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not show a specific regulated class, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF workflows process regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets
IF n8n retention or hosting region differs from the source system’s policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into workflows
Keep regulated data out of general-purpose workflows
Review n8n retention settings and backups
Pin hosting region to the required jurisdiction
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
